title: The Real Work/Life Balance: Setting Boundaries in the Workplace
coreMove: Work boundaries hold when you prepare the line before pressure arrives: name the request, script the response, and let systems protect time, energy, workload, and values.

exampleSpecs.audience: employees whose bosses test time off with quick calls
exampleSpecs.stakes: protect personal time without pretending the reporting relationship is equal
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show a vacation phone call from a boss becoming a prepared access boundary

exampleSpecs.audience: workers who soften away messages until they stop protecting leave
exampleSpecs.stakes: let the system hold the first line of the boundary
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show an out-of-office email using a return date and alternate route

exampleSpecs.audience: candidates who want to spot future boundary costs early
exampleSpecs.stakes: notice constant-availability norms before accepting the role
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show job hunting questions surfacing workload red flags

exampleSpecs.audience: employees facing value conflicts under client pressure
exampleSpecs.stakes: turn private discomfort into documented boundary language
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show ethical discomfort becoming a clear workplace boundary

exampleSpecs.audience: managers who equate exhaustion with commitment
exampleSpecs.stakes: use healthy local norms instead of inventing a risky speech from scratch
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show a colleague with healthy work-life balance becoming a practical model

exampleSpecs.audience: professionals repairing unclear availability after a weekend miss
exampleSpecs.stakes: reset access without surrendering every evening
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show work-life boundary advocacy after silence was treated as availability
